title: The Apollo 15 Rover
tagline: The first car on the Moon.
kicker: A true story from the Moon · 1971
mystery: How do you drive a car on the Moon?
stat.kg: kg of Moon rock and soil
stat.range: km from the lander, at most
p1.where: 30 July 1971. Falcon lands at the foot of the Apennine mountains.
p1.crew: Dave Scott and Jim Irwin: the seventh and eighth people to walk on the Moon.
p1.hello: Psst! I'm folded up on Falcon's side. I'm a car!
p1.first: The first car of my kind on the Moon. Let's go exploring!
p2.go: 31 July. First drive: all the way to the edge of Hadley Rille!
p2.hint: Use the arrow keys or the joystick. Bounce through each yellow ring!
p2.win: Hadley Rille! Elbow Crater, St. George, and all the way back.
p2.core: That drive was 10.3 km. A core sample came from 3 m under the surface.
p3.mountains: 1 August: 12.5 km along the foot of the Apennine Mountains.
p3.hint: Tap a crater name. When I get there, hold the button to bag the rock.
p3.s.bag: Into the bag! Moon rocks for scientists on Earth.
p3.s.bag2: Another one! Every rock is a page of the Moon's history.
p3.s.bag3: Bagged! My back is getting heavy.
p3.win: In three moonwalks they gathered 77.31 kg of rock and soil!
p3.west: 2 August: 5.1 km west, to Scarp Crater and along the rille.
p4.question: Here's a test. A hammer and a feather. Which one lands first?
p4.why: No air on the Moon to slow the feather. They fall at the same rate!
p5.memorial: They left a plaque and a small figure, for fourteen space explorers who died.
p5.time: 2 August 1971. After 66 hours 55 minutes, it's time to go.
p5.stay: Falcon's top half flies away. I stay here, parked for good.
p6.totals: Three moonwalks, 27.9 km, never more than 5 km from Falcon.
p6.bye: If you ever drive on the Moon, say hello. I'm still parked at Hadley.
